correctness.rationale: The source definition gives the roots of the canonical polynomial as fixed-cardinality root products. For a primitive core the root exponents are distinct base-\(Q\) subset sums below \(Q^d-1\); Frobenius is exactly cyclic rotation of the digit positions. This proves squarefreeness and identifies every irreducible factor with one rotation orbit. Möbius inversion gives the stated constant-weight necklace count. The independent checker reproduces the orbit counts for all \(2\le d\le10\) and exact binary-field factors for several primitive cores.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete structural factorization law for a newly introduced family of canonical Toeplitz recurrence polynomials over finite fields. It identifies every factor degree combinatorially, gives an exact factor-count formula, and shows that primitive cores still force reducibility in every interior exterior degree. This is a natural arithmetic boundary for recurrence decomposition rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a recomputation of a known table.
